source_text: Ὁμοίως πάλιν περὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ ὁρίζει ἐν ἄλλῳ προφήτῃ λέγοντι: Καὶ πότε ταῦτα συντελεσθήσεται; λέγει κύριος: ὅταν ξύλον κλιθῇ καὶ ἀναστῇ, καὶ ὅταν ἐκ ξύλου αἷμα στάξῃ. ἔχεις πάλιν περὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ καὶ τοῦ σταυροῦσθαι μέλλοντος. λέγει δὲ πάλιν τῷ Μωῡσῇ, πολεμουμένου τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀλλοφύλων, καὶ ἵνα ὑπομνήσῃ αὐτοὺς πολεμουμένους, ὅτι διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν παρεδόθησαν εἰς θάνατον: λέγει εἰς τὴν καρδίαν Μωϋσέως τὸ πνεῦμα, ἵνα ποιήσῃ τύπον σταυροῦ καὶ τοῦ μέλλοντος πάσχειν, ὅτι, ἐὰν μή, φησίν, ἐλπίσωσιν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα πολεμηθήσονται. τίθησιν οὖν Μωϋσῆς ἓν ἐφ̓ ἓν ὅπλον ἐν μέσῳ τῆς πυγμῆς, καὶ ὑψηλότερος σταθεὶς πάντων ἐξέτεινεν τὰς χεῖρας, καὶ οὕτως πάλιν ἐνίκα ὁ Ἰσραήλ. εἶτα, ὁπόταν καθεῖλεν, ἐθανατοῦντο. πρὸς τί; ἵνα γνῶσιν ὅτι οὐ δύνανται σωθῆναι, ἑὰν μὴ ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἐλπίσωσιν. καὶ πάλιν ἐν ἑτέρῳ προφήτῃ λέγει: Ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου πρὸς λαὸν ἀπειθῆ καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα ὁδῷ δικαίᾳ μου. πάλιν Μωϋσῆς ποιεῖ τύπον τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν παθεῖν, καὶ αὐτὸς ζωοποιήσει, ὃν δόξουσιν ἀπολωλεκέναι, ἐν σημείῳ πίπτοντος τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, ʽἐποίησεν γὰρ κύριος πάντα ὄφιν δάκνειν αὐτούς, καὶ ἀπέθνησκον ἐπειδὴ ἡ παράβασις διὰ τοῦ ὄφεως ἐν Εὔᾳ ἐγένετὀ. ἵνα ἐλέγξῃ αὐτούς. ὅτι διὰ τὴν παράβασιν αὐτῶν εἰς θλῖψιν θανάτου παραδοθήσονται. πέρας γέ τοι αὐτὸς Μωϋσῆς ἐντειλάμενος: Οὐκ ἔσται ὑμῖν οὔτε χωνευτὸν οὔτε γλυπτὸν εἰς θεὸν ὑμῖν. αὐτὸς ποιεῖ, ἵνα τύπον τοῦ Ἰησοῦ δείξῃ. ποιεῖ οὖν Μωϋσῆς χαλκοῦν ὄφιν καὶ τίθησιν ἐνδόξως καὶ κηρύγματι καλεῖ τὸν λαόν. ἐλθόντες οὖν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἐδέοντο Μωῦσέως, ἵνα περὶ αὐτῶν ἀνενέγκῃ δέησιν περὶ τῆς ἰάσεως αὐτῶν. εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς Μωϋσῆς: Ὅταν, φησίν. δηχθῇ τις ὑμῶν, ἐλθέτω ἐπὶ τὸν ὄφιν τὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ ξύλου ἐπικείμενον καὶ ἐλπισάτω πιστεύσας, ὅτι αὐτὸς ὢν νεκρὸς δύναται ζωοποιῆσαι, καὶ παραχρῆμα σωθήσεται. καὶ οὕτως ἐποίουν. ἔχεις πάλιν καὶ ἐν τούτοις τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ πάντα καὶ εἰς αὐτόν. τί λέγει πάλιν Μωϋσῆς Ἰησοῦ, υἱῷ Ναυή, ἐπιθεὶς αὐτῷ τοῦτο τὸ ὄνομα, ὄντι προφήτῃ, ἵνα μόνον ἀκούσῃ πᾶς ὁ λαός; ὅτι πάντα ὁ πατὴρ φανεροῖ περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ Ἰησοῦ. λέγει οὖν Μωϋσῆς Ἰησοῦ, υἱῷ Ναυή, ἐπιθεὶς τοῦτο τὸ ὄνομα, ὁπότε ἔπεμψεν αὐτὸν κατάσκοπον τῆς γῆς: Λάβε βιβλίον εἰς τὰς χεῖράς σου καὶ γράψον, ἃ λέγει κύριος, ὅτι ἐκκόψει ἐκ ῥιζῶν τὸν οἶκον πάντα τοῦ Ἀμαλὴκ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπ’ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν. ἴδε πάλιν Ἰησοῦς, οὐχὶ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου, ἀλλὰ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, τύπῳ δὲ ἐν σαρκὶ φανερωθείς. ἐπεὶ οὖν μέλλουσιν λέγειν, ὅτι Χριστὸς υἱὸς Δαυείδ ἐστιν, αὐτὸς προφητεύει Δαυείδ, φοβούμενος καὶ συνίων τὴν πλάνην τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν: Εἷπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου: Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου, ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου. καὶ πάλιν λέγει οὕτως Ἡσαΐας: Εἷπεν κύριος τῷ Χριστῷ μου κυρίῳ. οὗ ἐκράτησα τῆς δεξιᾶς αὐτοῦ, ἐπακοῦσαι ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ ἔθνη, καὶ ἰσχὺν βασιλέων διαρρήξω. ἴδε, πῶς Δαυεὶδ λέγει αὐτὸν κύριον. καὶ υἱὸν οὐ λέγει.
pass_a_gloss: Similarly again concerning the cross He defines in another prophet saying: And when will these things be fulfilled? says the Lord: when wood is bent and stands up, and when from wood blood drips. You have again concerning the cross and the one about to be crucified. And He says again to Moses, when Israel was being warred against by the aliens, and so that He might remind them, being warred against, that on account of their sins they were handed over to death: He says into the heart of Moses the Spirit, so that He might make a type of cross and of the one about to suffer, because, if not, He says, they will hope in Him, they will be warred against forever. Therefore Moses puts one upon one weapon in the middle of the fist, and having stood higher than all, he stretched out his hands, and thus again Israel was victorious. Then, as soon as he let down, they were being killed. Why? So that they might know that they are not able to be saved, if they do not hope in Him. And again in another prophet He says: The whole day I stretched out my hands to a disobedient people and one contradicting my righteous way. Again Moses makes a type of Jesus, because He must suffer, and He will make alive the one they think to have lost, in the sign of the falling of Israel, for the Lord made all a biting serpent to bite them, and they were dying, since the transgression through the serpent happened in Eve. So that He might convict them, because on account of their transgression they will be handed over to death's affliction. For Moses, having been commanded, says: There will not be for you either a molten or a carved thing for a god for you. He Himself does, so that He might show a type of Jesus. Therefore Moses makes a bronze serpent and puts it in a glorious and proclaimed way and calls the people. Having come therefore to the same place, they begged Moses, so that he might bring up a prayer concerning their healing. And Moses said to them: When anyone of you is bitten, let him come to the serpent on the wood hung and let him hope, having believed, that He, being dead, is able to make alive, and immediately he will be saved. And thus they were doing. You have again, also in these things, the glory of Jesus, because in Him are all things and to Him. What does Moses say again to Jesus, son of Nun, having put this name on him, being a prophet, so that the whole people might hear only? That the Father makes all things clear concerning the Son Jesus. Therefore Moses says to Jesus, son of Nun, having put this name on him, when he sent him as a spy of the land: Take a book into your hands and write what the Lord says, because He will cut off from the roots the whole house of Amalek, the Son of God, in the last of the days. See again Jesus, not a son of man, but a Son of God, having been revealed in flesh in type. Since therefore they are about to say that Christ is a son of David, He Himself prophesies through David, fearing and understanding the error of the sinners: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies as a footstool under your feet. And again Isaiah says thus: The Lord said to my Christ, the Lord, whose right hand I held, to hear before Him the nations, and I will tear the strength of kings. See, how David calls Him Lord. And he does not call Him son.

pass_b_english: In the same way, he defines the cross once more through another prophet, who says: "And when will these things be fulfilled?" The Lord answers: "When wood is bent and stands up, and when blood drips from wood." Here again you have a reference to the cross and to the one who is about to be crucified.

He also speaks again to Moses when Israel was being warred against by foreigners. He wanted to remind them, while they were being attacked, that they had been handed over to death because of their sins. The Spirit spoke into Moses' heart, telling him to make a type of the cross and of the one who was going to suffer. The Spirit said, "If they do not hope in him, they will be warred against forever." So Moses placed one weapon on top of another in the middle of the battle, stood higher than everyone, and stretched out his hands. Thus Israel prevailed again. But whenever he lowered his hands, they were killed. Why? So that they would know they cannot be saved unless they hope in him.

And again in another prophet he says: "All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people who walk in a way that is not right." Once more Moses makes a type of Jesus, because he must suffer, and he will give life to the one they think has perished. This happens in the sign of Israel's fall, for the Lord sent serpents to bite them all, and they were dying, since the transgression came through the serpent in Eve. He did this to convict them, because on account of their transgression they will be handed over to the affliction of death. For Moses, after being commanded, says: "You shall not have for yourselves either a molten or a carved image as a god." Yet he himself makes one, so that he might show a type of Jesus. So Moses makes a bronze serpent and sets it up gloriously, and with a proclamation he calls the people. When they came together, they begged Moses to offer a prayer for their healing. Moses said to them: "When any of you is bitten, let him come to the serpent hanging on the wood, and let him hope, believing that he, though dead, is able to give life, and immediately he will be saved." And so they did. Here again, in these things, you have the glory of Jesus, because all things are in him and for him.

What does Moses say again to Jesus, son of Nun, after giving him this name, he being a prophet, so that all the people might hear? He declares that the Father makes everything clear concerning the Son Jesus. So Moses says to Jesus, son of Nun, after giving him this name, when he sent him as a spy of the land: "Take a book into your hands and write what the Lord says, because the Son of God will cut off from the roots the whole house of Amalek in the last days." See again: Jesus, not a son of man, but the Son of God, revealed in the flesh as a type. Since they are about to say that the Christ is a son of David, he himself prophesies through David, fearing and understanding the error of the sinners: "The Lord said to my Lord, 'Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet'" (Psalm 110:1). And again Isaiah says: "The Lord said to my Christ, the Lord, whose right hand I held, to hear before him the nations, and I will tear the strength of kings" (Isaiah 45:1). See how David calls him Lord, and does not call him son.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological arguments regarding the typology of the cross, the bronze serpent, and the Davidic messianic prophecies. Pass A preserves all clauses and nuances of the Greek. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that remains faithful to the source. Scripture citations (Psalm 110:1 and Isaiah 45:1) are correctly identified in Pass B based on the quoted text.
